hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history and views of Indian River waterways
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years and offers views of the Indian River.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse stands as a red brick tower that has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years since its construction in 1860. The historic landmark rises high above the inlet, serving as a testament to the navigational aids that have protected mariners traveling these coastal waters for generations.

The 105-step climb takes visitors up a narrow spiral staircase to the top gallery. Lighthouse keepers once made this same climb night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that continues to shine for mariners navigating the area. The physical journey upward through the tower connects modern visitors to the dedicated keepers who performed their duties in this same space throughout the lighthouse's long operational history.

From the gallery at the top, visitors experience breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding waterways and coastline. The Atlantic Ocean stretches to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel, and the sea breeze provides relief from warm Florida mornings. The elevated vantage point offers a commanding perspective of how these waterways intersect and the strategic importance of the lighthouse's location for maritime navigation.

The site includes a museum with restored historic buildings on the grounds that detail the lighthouse's fascinating past. The exhibits cover the structure's construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. Visitors can walk among the historic buildings and learn about the various chapters in the lighthouse's operational history. The combination of the tower climb and the museum grounds provides a comprehensive look at how this navigational beacon served the Atlantic coast and the keepers who maintained it through different eras of American history.

cards.headline: New Aldi opens in Hobe Sound as grocery prices rise 2.8% this year
cards.teaser: A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, offering Martin County shoppers an affordable option as food prices contin.
cards.body:
A new Aldi grocery store opened Thursday at 8867 Southeast Bridge Road in Hobe Sound, bringing more affordable choices to Martin County shoppers. Customers Cheryl and Tony Cooperman said they are excited to have the store close to their home. Cheryl Cooperman said grocery prices are getting expensive and are starting to change the way she shops. She said they are the type of people who never used to look at prices, but now she will go with what is on sale instead of just what they want, something they never used to do.

The opening comes as the USDA expects grocery prices to rise 2.8% this year. Egg prices are dropping, and beef prices fell 1.3% from April to May, though wholesale beef prices remain at all-time highs for this time of year. Pork rose 1% from April to May, and chicken prices rose 1.3% over the same period. Fruits and vegetables are seeing an increase of less than 1%. Shoppers James and Harry said Thursday they do not expect relief at the register anytime soon, predicting prices will stay inflated. They said stores like Aldi, which often have lower prices than other stores, can make a difference for everyday shoppers because nobody is immune from feeling the price increase.

cards.headline: Florida's 32-day back-to-school sales tax holiday begins July 20, offering families savings on clothing, supplies, computers
cards.body:
Florida families can save on essential school items during the state's annual back-to-school sales tax holiday, which runs from July 20 through Aug. 20, 2026. The 32-day tax-free shopping period eliminates sales tax on qualifying purchases, with a family spending $500 on eligible items saving $35 in sales tax.

Clothing items under $100 per item qualify for the exemption, including shirts, pants, dresses, shoes, uniforms and athletic wear. Backpacks, handbags, diaper bags and fanny packs also qualify, along with accessories like wallets, belts, ties and graduation caps and gowns. Briefcases, suitcases, watches, jewelry, skis, swim fins, roller blades and any clothing item over $100 do not qualify. School supplies under $50 per item are tax-free, including pens, pencils, erasers, crayons, notebooks, binders, folders, construction paper, poster board, markers, scissors, glue, tape, staplers, lunch boxes and composition books. Blank CDs also qualify. Learning aids and puzzles under $30 per item qualify, covering flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets.

Computers and accessories under $1,500 per item are exempt from sales tax, including laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators. Tax-free accessories include keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use, as business purchases do not qualify. The tax exemption does not apply at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, public lodging establishments or airports. Items normally sold together must be purchased as a set and cannot be split up to meet price thresholds.

Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. Exchanges for the same item in a different size or color remain tax-free, and items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday period are exempt from sales tax. Gift cards can be used to buy eligible items tax-free during the holiday regardless of when the gift card was purchased. Items qualify if families take delivery during the holiday period or put eligible items on layaway during the holiday, even if final payment comes later. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast Traffic Report: Major Ramp and Road Closures Planned July 12-17
cards.teaser:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Driv
cards.body:
Motorists should prepare for overnight interstate ramp closures, extended neighborhood road closures and lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

Drivers across the Treasure Coast could encounter delays during the week of July 10-17 as construction and maintenance continue on several major roadways.

The Florida Department of Transportation's latest weekly traffic report identifies multiple lane restrictions across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties. FDOT placed additional emphasis on full road, ramp and bridge closures expected to have the greatest effect on motorists.

MAJOR CLOSURES TO KNOW ABOUT

I-95 exit to Bridge Road closing overnight in Martin County

The southbound Interstate 95 exit ramp to County Road 708, also known as Bridge Road, at Exit 96 will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.

Drivers will be directed to exit at Kanner Highway, travel south on Pratt Whitney Road and then head east on Bridge Road.

The closure is needed for roadway construction. Weather-related contingency dates are scheduled for July 19-23.

Port St. Lucie neighborhood roads could close for several days

Extended closures are planned along several side streets near the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project.

Closures may begin at 7 a.m. Monday, July 13, and continue until 5 p.m. Friday, July 17, on portions of SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road and SW McHord Avenue.

The roads will close intermittently for drainage and utility installation. FDOT said adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Detours will generally use SW Paar Drive, SW McCain Street, SW McIntyre Street, SW Kabane Street and other nearby roads, depending on the closure location.

I-95 ramp to Orange Avenue closing in Fort Pierce

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to westbound State Road 68, or Orange Avenue, will be closed from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, July 12, through Thursday, July 16.

Motorists will be detoured using the exit to eastbound Orange Avenue, northbound Jenkins Road and westbound Loop Road before returning to westbound Orange Avenue.

The work includes paving and lighting installation. Contingency dates are July 19-23.

MARTIN COUNTY TRAFFIC IMPACTS

Motorists should expect overnight lane closures on I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line. Up to two lanes may close in each direction during overnight hours for milling, resurfacing and signage work.

On U.S. 1 in Stuart, two lanes may close intermittently between Fischer Street and Decker Avenue from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday for sign installation.

A1A between Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may be reduced to one lane at times from Monday through Friday for drainage work and pavement widening. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic through the work zone.

Martin Highway between Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard may also have intermittent overnight lane closures Tuesday through Thursday.

FDOT is additionally warning drivers in advance about several upcoming I-95 ramp closures at Martin Highway and Kanner Highway later in July and early August.

ST. LUCIE COUNTY TRAFFIC IMPACTS

Port St. Lucie Boulevard between Seafury Lane and Lennard Road may have daytime lane closures Monday through Friday. Two lanes may close overnight from Sunday through Friday for drainage work, milling and repaving.

U.S. 1 between Jennings Road and Golden Oak Trail may also have lane restrictions during both daytime and overnight hours.

On SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard, one lane may close between Jordin Avenue and Alcantarra Boulevard from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday as crews continue the widening project.

Up to two lanes may close overnight on I-95 between Glades Cut-Off Road and the area just south of Okeechobee Road for milling and repaving.

Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may continue to have intermittent weekday lane closures through September as part of the roadway widening project.

NORTH CAUSEWAY MARINE RESTRICTIONS

The new A1A North Causeway Bridge remains open to vehicle traffic, but significant restrictions are planned for boaters using the Intracoastal Waterway.

The existing drawbridge will not open to marine traffic from 7 a.m. Thursday, July 16, through 6 p.m. Saturday, July 18. Boats capable of passing beneath the bridge without an opening may continue through.

Additional single-leaf openings, partial channel obstructions and temporary full channel closures are scheduled through July 24 as crews remove portions of the former drawbridge.

FDOT said the marine work will not affect vehicle traffic on the new bridge.

INDIAN RIVER COUNTY TRAFFIC IMPACTS

One lane may remain closed on the 17th Street bridges between Indian River Boulevard and Indian Bay Drive as bridge rehabilitation continues.

At the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road, one or two interstate lanes may close overnight Sunday through Thursday for bridge work, milling and resurfacing.

On 90th Avenue between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street, one lane may close overnight Sunday through Friday for construction associated with the 85th Street widening project.

Drivers traveling near Sebastian Inlet should also expect intermittent lane or shoulder closures on A1A through Friday, July 17. Flaggers will direct motorists through the work zone.

Sections of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park will remain closed during construction of the new bridge. The closures are expected to continue through spring 2032, although the park and portions of both parking lots remain open.

PLAN AHEAD

Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Motorists should allow additional travel time, follow posted detours and use caution around workers and equipment.

Real-time interstate traffic conditions are available through Florida 511. Updated lane closure information is also available through FDOT District Four.

cards.headline: Woman charged after inhaling nitrous oxide in Port St. Lucie Police Department parking lot
cards.body:
A woman faces charges after authorities say she was inhaling nitrous oxide in the parking lot of the Port St. Lucie Police Department. The incident occurred Thursday at the police facility.

The woman was arrested and charged following the incident in the department parking lot. Port St. Lucie Police responded to the situation at their own headquarters.

Nitrous oxide, also known as laughing gas, is a controlled substance that can result in criminal charges when inhaled for recreational purposes. The arrest took place in the parking lot of the police station itself.

The woman now faces criminal charges related to the inhaling of the substance. The Port St. Lucie Police Department handled the arrest at their facility.

cards.headline: Homeland Security task force charges dozens in South Florida with federal firearms and drug trafficking crimes
cards.teaser: Federal authorities charged dozens of people in South Florida with firearms and drug trafficking offenses and seized 94 firearms in a Homeland Security operation.
cards.body:
A Homeland Security task force charged dozens of individuals in South Florida with federal firearms and drug trafficking crimes. The operation resulted in the seizure of 94 firearms.

The Department of Justice announced the charges Thursday following the multi-agency law enforcement operation. Authorities targeted individuals involved in illegal weapons possession and drug distribution networks across South Florida.

The task force seized a total of 94 firearms during the operation. Federal prosecutors are pursuing charges against the defendants for violations of federal firearms and drug trafficking laws.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranked 67th most stressed city in United States
hero.teaser: A WalletHub study released this month found Port St. Lucie is the 67th most stressed city in the United States and the 42nd most financially stressed city in America.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States according to a WalletHub study released this month. The report cited Port St. Lucie as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics including average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates.

Jacksonville ranked as the most stressed city in Florida at number 37 nationally. In South Florida, Miami ranked 50th with affordable housing listed as fourth worst in the United States. Fort Lauderdale ranked 83rd. Florida had no cities in the top 35 most stressed.

WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. He noted that some stress comes from issues with family, friends or employers that people cannot control, but where someone lives can significantly impact their stress levels. Lupo said it is important to consider how a city may affect mental health when moving, not just financial opportunities. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities. On the opposite end, Fremont, California ranked as the least stressed city in the nation. Located in the Bay Area, Fremont is a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million. South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota followed as cities with the lowest stress levels.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova defeats Coco Gauff to reach Wimbledon final after dramatic tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday, becoming the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final.
hero.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, champion in 2024.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

cards.headline: Women's Professional Baseball League unveils team names and logos ahead of inaugural season
cards.teaser: The Women's Professional Baseball League announced the nicknames and logos of its four teams ahead of its debut season starting August 1, with each team name inspired by pioneering women.
cards.body:
The Women's Professional Baseball League unveiled the nicknames and logos of its four teams on Wednesday ahead of its inaugural season. Each team name was inspired by pioneering women. Kelsie Whitmore, the first overall pick in the WPBL's inaugural draft, will play for the San Francisco Firebells. Mo'ne Davis will play center field for the Los Angeles Queens, along with veteran Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato.

The league also includes the New York Heights and the Boston Hunters. The WPBL's debut season begins on August 1 in Springfield, Illinois. Games will be played at Robin Roberts Stadium and will run through the second half of September, including a regular season and playoffs.

The New York Heights were inspired by Dorothy Irene Height, a pioneering civil rights and women's rights leader from New York. The San Francisco Firebells were inspired by Lillie Hitchcock Coit, known as Firebelle, who was a champion of San Francisco's volunteer firefighters. The Los Angeles Queens were created after Lizzie Murphy, a baseball pioneer known as the Queen of the Diamond. The Boston Hunters are inspired by Harriot K. Hunt, a pioneering Boston physician and women's rights activist.

cards.headline: Park Vista Community High School football team targets state playoffs after strong finish to 2025 season
cards.body:
Park Vista Community High School's football team is building on late-season momentum as the Cobras set their sights on the state playoffs in 2026. The Cobras struggled to find their footing early in 2025, but finished strong, winning four of their last five games. Senior Harris Bender said it felt good throughout the second half of that season. The team is working towards being able to carry that through the whole season, and they have all the pieces in place now. It is just about executing. Senior Erik Lee said coming in, he feels like they got the guys that they need to get it done, but also they got to put the work in to get there as well.

The ultimate goal is the state playoffs and eventually a state title, something the program has not achieved since 2017. Park Vista head football coach Donald Hanna said they got to take it one game at a time. The team can't look past anyone. They got to handle business weekly and if they do that, do their job, that will get them in the playoffs. Senior Justice Jones said it is going to feel amazing, because he already knows it is gonna happen. Park Vista opens the 2026 season on the road against Atlantic in August.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
The 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival will return to Vero Beach this November, according to Under The Sun Promotions, Inc.

The festival is hosted by Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. The event will be held in Vero Beach in November 2026.

The Treasure Coast Seafood Festival is an annual event that has been held for 17 previous years. This will mark the 18th year of the festival in Vero Beach.

Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. is organizing the event. Additional details about specific dates, location, and festival activities have not been released.

Blank CDs also qualify. Learning aids and puzzles under $30 per item qualify, covering flashcards, learning cards, jigsaw puzzles, puzzle books, interactive books, educational toys, memory and matching games, stacking blocks and educational sets.

Computers and accessories under $1,500 per item are exempt from sales tax, including laptops, desktops, tablets, electronic book readers and calculators. Tax-free accessories include keyboards, mice, monitors without TV tuners, printers, ink cartridges, modems, routers, cables, educational and productivity software, storage devices and memory cards. Computers must be for personal, non-commercial use, as business purchases do not qualify. The tax exemption does not apply at theme parks, entertainment complexes, hotels, public lodging establishments or airports. Items normally sold together must be purchased as a set and cannot be split up to meet price thresholds.

Items ordered online during the holiday period qualify for the exemption even if delivered after Aug. 20. Exchanges for the same item in a different size or color remain tax-free, and items purchased with rain checks issued during the holiday period are exempt from sales tax. Gift cards can be used to buy eligible items tax-free during the holiday regardless of when the gift card was purchased. Items qualify if families take delivery during the holiday period or put eligible items on layaway during the holiday, even if final payment comes later. Florida retailers have no option to opt out of the sales tax holiday, and all qualifying purchases must be processed tax-free during the designated period.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in US, 42nd in financial stress
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie ranked as the 67th most stressed city in the United States, according to a WalletHub study released this month. The report cited Port St. Lucie as the 42nd most financially stressed city in America.

WalletHub compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. Florida performed fairly well overall, with no cities in the top 35 most stressed. Jacksonville ranked as the most stressed city in Florida at number 37 in the nation. In South Florida, Miami ranked 50th most stressed nationally, with affordable housing fourth worst in the U.S., and Fort Lauderdale ranked 83rd.

Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the nation. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. He noted that while some stress is out of our control due to issues with family, friends or employers, where you live can play a big role in how stressed you are. Lupo emphasized that when moving, it's important to consider how a certain city may impact your mental health, not just your financial opportunities.

The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors. Fremont, California topped the list of least stressed cities. Located in the Bay Area, Fremont is a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million. South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota followed as the next least stressed cities in the country.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history and views of Indian River waterways
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years and offers views of the Indian River.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse stands as a red brick tower that has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years since its construction in 1860. The historic landmark rises high above the inlet, serving as a testament to the navigational aids that have protected mariners traveling these coastal waters for generations.

The 105-step climb takes visitors up a narrow spiral staircase to the top gallery. Lighthouse keepers once made this same climb night after night to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that continues to shine for mariners navigating the area. The physical journey upward through the tower connects modern visitors to the dedicated keepers who performed their duties in this same space throughout the lighthouse's long operational history.

From the gallery at the top, visitors experience breathtaking panoramic views of the surrounding waterways and coastline. The Atlantic Ocean stretches to the east, while the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers below. Boats glide through the channel, and the sea breeze provides relief from warm Florida mornings. The elevated vantage point offers a commanding perspective of how these waterways intersect and the strategic importance of the lighthouse's location for maritime navigation.

The site includes a museum with restored historic buildings on the grounds that detail the lighthouse's fascinating past. The exhibits cover the structure's construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. Visitors can walk among the historic buildings and learn about the various chapters in the lighthouse's operational history. The combination of the tower climb and the museum grounds provides a comprehensive look at how this navigational beacon served the Atlantic coast and the keepers who maintained it through different eras of American history.
